pr_title: Rewrite reference processing code in preparation for opening/closing from comment references
pr_body:
This PR does the following:

* Rearrange the code used for parsing mentions (`@user`) and cross-references (`#123`, etc.) in issues, pull requests, comments and commits.
* Provide code to properly parse/skip Markdown code in the contents.
	* Currently reference processing ignores any Markdown code, so references are parsed even in code blocks and other markup that shouldn't; for example:
```
	This code `mike @mike` should not count as a mention.
```
* Process all references in one place (issues, PRs, comments, commits, HTML rendering).
* Fix #8259

Although this PR has value on itself, the goal is to set the base for properly processing closing/reopening keywords in a future PR.

## Progress (done)

- [x] Create a markdown stripper class
- [x] Move reference detection from `models` into `modules/references`
- [x] Detection of closing/reopening keywords in the new `references` module
- [x] Generate content references to facilitate HTML markup insertion
- [x] Make `markup/html.go` use the `references` module so all reference parsing resides in one place.
- [x] Make `markup/html.go` aware of closes/fixes keywords to render an indication for that.
- [x] Support highlight of action keywords like "closes", "reopens", etc.
- [x] Should fix --- #7810 but I'm unable to reproduce

#### In another, future PR

- [ ] Close/reopen issues from PR comments.

issue_context.title: Commits should consider user permissions when creating comments on referenced issues
issue_context.body:
- Gitea version (or commit ref): 1.9.3

## Description

Currently `UpdateIssuesCommit()` creates a cross-reference comment on another repository even if the user has no permission whatsoever on it.

https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/blob/63ff61615ec6aaa25887f8ce605c9082c106a34b/models/action.go#L572-L600

review_comments: Because this is TestUpdateIssuesCommit_AnotherRepoNoPermission(); the user has in fact no rights to create that comment (it was created before, but it was wrong IMHO).
